NOT GATED ON /hasGovernmentSponsoredCoverage: a return-level annual bar would be WRONG-GRAINED, since Pub. 974 scopes eligibility per month and per individual ("You generally cannot take the PTC for an individual in your tax family FOR ANY MONTH that the individual is eligible for MEC", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p974.pdf, page 8) — a filer with Marketplace coverage Jan-Jun and Medicaid Jul-Dec would lose all six legitimate coverage months under a single whole-family, whole-year Boolean. Such a bar would also delete the IRC 36B(f)(2) excess-APTC reconciliation this fact gates through /hasPtcQualifyingPlan, /needsToFileForm8962 and the whole Form 8962 chain, though IRC 36B(f)(2)(A) makes the excess an INCREASE IN TAX regardless of eligibility (26 U.S.C. 36B, https://uscode.house.gov/view.xhtml?req=granuleid:USC-2024-title26-section36B&num=0&edition=2024) and the 2025 Instructions for Form 8962 require it: "If APTC was paid for you or an individual in your tax family, you must file Form 8962 to reconcile (compare) this APTC with your PTC. If the APTC is more than your PTC, you have excess APTC" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8962.pdf, page 2).
/writableHasGovernmentSponsoredCoverage and /hasGovernmentSponsoredCoverage stay in the module, but are READ BY NOTHING here — a declared gap. A per-month, per-individual rebuild of the IRC 36B(c)(2)(B) bar — a per-1095A-month / per-tax-family-member eligibility test feeding the twelve monthly PTC legs, never /needsToFileForm8962 and never the repayment path — is named as future work, not built here.

Fact.Name: A dependent must file and Form 8962 line 2b is missing
Fact.Description:
A PTC return that claims at least one dependent, says at least one of them is required to file their own return, and has NOT given the combined modified AGI that Form 8962 line 2b needs. It is a flow knockout and it refuses only that residue: line 2b itself is built (/writablePtcDependentsModifiedAgi, read by /householdIncome through the complete-safe wrapper /ptcDependentsModifiedAgiOrZero), so a return that supplies the figure files normally and its household income foots.
WHY THE UNANSWERED CASE STAYS REFUSED rather than defaulting. /ptcDependentsModifiedAgiOrZero reads an unanswered line 2b as $0, which is the right answer for the large population with no dependent required to file and the WRONG one here: it would understate household income, which raises the credit. The refusal is the only thing standing between this return and an overstated credit, so it is the correct permanent refusal for as long as the figure is missing.

Fact.Name: Form 8962 Part IV is required and its intake is not finished
Fact.Description:
A return that must allocate policy amounts with another taxpayer AND has not supplied the Part IV intake that lets this graph do it. It is a flow knockout, and it refuses only that residue: the allocation itself is built, so a return that names a usable allocation row for every shared policy files normally, and the three allocated amounts reach Form 8962 lines 12 through 23.
WHAT IS LEFT REFUSED, and why each case is the correct refusal rather than a gap. (1) The filer says an additional enrolled person belongs to a different tax family, or that they are enrolled with another family, and NO Form 1095-A names an allocation row this graph can apply — the return says a policy is shared and does not say how. (2) A Form 1095-A names a row whose three percentage columns are all unanswered. Reading either as "no allocation" would hand the filer the whole policy amount, which is a silent 100 percent allocation of a policy they have told this graph they share. /allocationIntakeIsComplete carries both tests and names the one thing this graph still cannot distinguish, the allocation SITUATION.

Fact.Name: The entered Form 1095-A documents must be reconciled before filing
Fact.Description: Whether the TP's repeated Form 1095-A group inventory still needs reconciliation, or an entered Form 1095-A has its VOID box checked. A VOID form means the earlier Form 1095-A for that policy was sent in error, and neither the VOID form nor the earlier one is used to complete Form 8962; both must be deleted before the return files. SCREEN (VOID arm): "One of the Forms 1095-A you entered has its VOID box checked. That means the earlier Form 1095-A for the same policy was sent in error. Delete both the VOID form and the earlier form for that policy; neither one is used to figure your premium tax credit." Only a return on which the Form 1095-A amounts can reach Form 8962 is blocked (/hasPtcQualifyingPlan and /applicableTaxPayerOrHasAptc, the gates the reconciliation arm uses).

Household income for PTC, Form 8962 line 3: line 2a plus line 2b, where line 2a is TAXPAYER/SPOUSE MAGI (= /ptcMagi, the taxpayer's AGI + tax-exempt interest + non-taxable social security) and line 2b is the total MAGI of all dependents required to file, WIRED through /ptcDependentsModifiedAgiOrZero, the complete-safe wrapper of the /writablePtcDependentsModifiedAgi intake. A return with a dependent who is required to file is also knocked out of submission by /dependentsRequiredToFile (flow /flowIsKnockedOut), so that population is gated as well as computed. THE KNOCKOUT BOUNDS THE SCOPE, not the arithmetic: this fact is Form 8962 line 3, "Add lines 2a and 2b", literally. interpretation:provisional (the knockout, not the arithmetic, is what still bounds the scope).

Fact.Name: Form 8962 line 2b, the dependents' modified AGI, complete safe
Fact.Description:
The complete safe wrapper of /writablePtcDependentsModifiedAgi: the filer's Form 8962 line 2b entry when it was answered, and $0 otherwise. It is the line 2b term of /householdIncome, which prints Form 8962 line 3, "Add lines 2a and 2b". The intake is a bare Writable, so a raw Dependency on it would make household income, the applicable figure, the contribution amount and the whole premium tax credit Incomplete on every PTC return that has no dependent required to file, which is nearly all of them.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO. It does not retire ptc:/dependentsRequiredToFile, the knockout that refuses a return with a dependent who is required to file; that refusal is untouched and still gates the population. Before this wrapper existed the line 2b intake printed on Form 8962 and reached no total, so a return that answered it computed the credit on an understated household income and an overstated credit. It now foots. $0 on every committed scenario, so household income and the credit are byte identical.

How much of your Jan enrollment premium (the portion you were responsible for) remained unpaid as of the unextended due date of your return? i8962 (2025) states that for any month you were covered, did not pay your share of the premiums, and are allowed a monthly credit amount, the enrollment premium you use to compute your monthly credit amount must be reduced by any portion of the premium that is unpaid as of the unextended due date for filing your return for the tax year that includes the month. Asked when: Jan is named in this Form 1095-A's /1095As/*/writableRetainedUnpaidMonths (a month you have confirmed you are keeping as a coverage month under one of Publication 974's three retention scenarios despite an unpaid premium). Unanswered posture: complete-safe $0 reduction — the enrollment premium computes as entered, unreduced, the same posture this dictionary uses for every other as-yet-unquantified attestation on this axis; the retention answer itself already establishes enough was paid to avoid termination, so the residual unpaid amount is disclosed as a favourable default rather than a hard stop. Validation: Dollar, Min $0 (cannot exceed the entered enrollment premium in substance, though no Max is enforced here — a filer entering more than the premium itself is a data-entry error the return process can still catch). Feeds: /1095As/*/ptcMonthlyPremiumJan (Form 8962 Part II column (a), the enrollment premium for Jan), floored at $0.

Fact.Name: Repeated-policy SLCSP reconciliation groups
Fact.Description: One row per repeated marketplace-state and coverage-family group. A group consolidates every Form 1095-A that represents the same policy/coverage family across the year. The application assigns the stable group key (for example NJ-1), records the marketplace state, and prefills one reconciled column (b) benchmark per month.

Fact.Name: All repeated-policy SLCSP groups have been identified
Fact.Description: Confirm that every Form 1095-A has been reviewed for repeated-policy groups and that every repeated group has a row. This is a completeness answer, not a statement that any particular group exists; answer Yes when all Forms 1095-A have been classified.

Fact.Name: Stable repeated-policy group key
Fact.Description: SERVICE-assigned stable key for this repeated policy/coverage-family group, for example NJ-1. The same key is written to each member Form 1095-A. This is not a filer-entered identifier.

Fact.Name: Marketplace state for the repeated-policy group
Fact.Description: Select the marketplace state recorded on the group; the application prefills this from the member Forms 1095-A.

Some but not all Forms 1095-A carry a reconciliation group key
Fact.Description: Whether this return's Forms 1095-A mix an answered repeated-policy group key with an unanswered one. The application's own intake rule is all-or-nothing: once any Form 1095-A carries a group key, every Form 1095-A must carry one, and a form with no same-marketplace- state partner still gets its own, unique key. A return caught mid-keying cannot be trusted to compute the SLCSP benchmark correctly, because an unkeyed same-state partner would add its own full column (b) amount alongside an already-reconciled group total. Blocks submission until every Form 1095-A carries a key.

Did you check your correct SLCSP premium for this Form 1095-A using the Marketplace's Tax Tool or Publication 974? You entered $0 for the applicable second lowest cost silver plan (SLCSP) premium on this Form 1095-A. Column B of Form 1095-A may be wrong, left blank, or reported as -0- whenever no advance payment of the premium tax credit was made for the coverage, or when you had a change in circumstances you did not report to the Marketplace. To determine the correct amount, see Publication 974 or, if you enrolled through the federally facilitated Marketplace, go to HealthCare.gov/Tax-Tool/. Asked when: any monthly or the annual applicable SLCSP premium entered for this Form 1095-A (Form 8962 Part II column (b), lines 11 or 12-23) equals exactly $0.00 — a positive entry never triggers this question, and neither does a month the separate premium-paid disallowance rule (26 USC 36B(c)(2)(A)(ii)) has already removed from the coverage-month count, since that month's column (b) reads $0 regardless of the entered figure. Unanswered posture: the return does not compute a premium tax credit for the affected coverage — this Form 1095-A, and the return overall, are treated as Incomplete rather than silently filing a $0 credit for that Form 1095-A's coverage months, because a $0 or blank column B is common (it occurs whenever no APTC was paid) and the instructions place the duty to correct it on the filer. Validation: Boolean (Yes/No); answering Yes lets the entered $0 figure compute as filed; answering No does not itself change the figure — it signals the filer must return to the Form 1095-A entry and correct the SLCSP premium before the credit can compute. Feeds: /1095As/*/hasEnteredAllMonthlySlcsp (monthly path) and the annual-SLCSP completeness gate that reads /1095As/*/writableSlcspAnnualPremium.

Fact.Name: Policy start and termination dates are within tax year 2025
Fact.Description:
Value-level guard for Form 1095-A policy dates. The Exchange coverage period used by this TY2025 dictionary must fall within 2025; a date outside the year must not be reduced to its month and silently create a 2025 coverage month. This guard complements the writable Day limits, which are enforced by the JVM validator but are not sufficient on the default Scala.js path.
THIS All CARRIES NO IsComplete CONJUNCTS ON start OR end: it is purely the VALUE test. An IsComplete(start)/IsComplete(end) pair would make an UNANSWERED policy date resolve this guard Complete FALSE - and because every ../policyIsActiveIn<Month> reads All(../policyDatesWithinTaxYear, ../policyStartsIn<Month>), false dominates and all twelve coverage months would go Complete FALSE too, so a HALF-ENTERED 1095-A would silently compute zero coverage months and $0 PTC on a printed line instead of staying Incomplete and driving the interview - house rule 5 verbatim, on a computation input rather than a refusal guard.
With both dates answered, a date outside 2025 resolves this guard Complete FALSE; with either date UNANSWERED the comparisons are Incomplete, the All is Incomplete, and Incomplete propagates to the twelve months and to ../hasPolicyForAllMonths, which is the base posture.
POSTURE, STATED (house rule 5): Incomplete on an unanswered date, Complete FALSE on an out-of-year date.

Fact.Name: This policy's enrollment premium for January, before any Part IV allocation
Fact.Description: This Form 1095-A's own enrollment premium for January, as the Marketplace reported it and as this graph derives it from the annual figure or the monthly entry. It is the figure a policy the filer did NOT share with another taxpayer carries all the way to the return, and the base the Part IV allocation percentage multiplies where the policy IS shared: ../ptcMonthlyPremiumJan is that multiplication, and every reader of this policy's January reads THAT fact, not this one.

Fact.Name: This policy's January enrollment premium after the government-MEC adjustment
Fact.Description: Uses the adjusted coverage-family amount only for an affected January; otherwise preserves ../preGovernmentMecPtcMonthlyPremiumJan. No fallback exists when the eligibility result or required adjusted amount is incomplete.

Fact.Name: This policy's enrollment premium for January, after any Part IV allocation
Fact.Description:
This Form 1095-A's enrollment premium for January as it enters the return: the policy's own figure at ../unallocatedPtcMonthlyPremiumJan, multiplied by the Part IV column (e) allocation percentage when this policy is linked to an allocation row that covers January and that column is answered, and the whole figure otherwise. Form 8962 lines 12 through 23, column (a) prints the sum of this fact across the return's Forms 1095-A.
THE PASS-THROUGH ARM IS NOT A FALLBACK, it is the answer for two different populations: a policy nobody shared, and a shared policy where column (e) is blank, which the source allows whenever the allocation situation does not allocate the enrollment premiums. Both keep the whole figure, and neither is a silent 100 percent allocation — an allocation row whose month range cannot be read does not resolve at all (../policyAllocationRowResolves), and /needsAllocations still refuses that return.
ROUNDING: the product is a Dollar and carries cents, TRUNCATED rather than rounded half-up at the third decimal (8500/12 = 708.33 times one half is 354.165 and this fact carries 354.16). The line that prints it, Form 8962 lines 12 through 23, applies Round to the sum across policies afterwards, so the truncation is invisible except where a month's allocated share lands on a .495 boundary.
THE WHEN IS ALWAYS COMPLETE: ../policyAllocationAppliesInJan is an always-Complete Boolean and the second conjunct is an IsComplete test, so the Switch never collapses to a Placeholder on a return whose allocation intake is half answered.

This Form 1095-A's applicable SLCSP premium for December as it enters the return: the policy's own figure at ../unallocatedPtcMonthlySlcspPremiumDec, multiplied by the Part IV column (f) allocation percentage when this policy is linked to an allocation row that covers December and that column is answered, and the whole figure otherwise. Form 8962 lines 12 through 23, column (b) prints the sum of this fact across the return's Forms 1095-A.
THE PASS-THROUGH ARM IS NOT A FALLBACK, it is the answer for two different populations: a policy nobody shared, and a shared policy where column (f) is blank, which is the ORDINARY case rather than an omission: the source enters a column (f) percentage only under Allocation Situations 1 and 4, and directs every other situation to determine the correct applicable SLCSP premium for the coverage family and enter THAT on lines 12 through 23, column (b) — which is the entered monthly figure this fact passes through. Both keep the whole figure, and neither is a silent 100 percent allocation — an allocation row whose month range cannot be read does not resolve at all (../policyAllocationRowResolves), and /needsAllocations still refuses that return.
ROUNDING: the product is a Dollar and carries cents, TRUNCATED rather than rounded half-up at the third decimal (8500/12 = 708.33 times one half is 354.165 and this fact carries 354.16). The line that prints it, Form 8962 lines 12 through 23, applies Round to the sum across policies afterwards, so the truncation is invisible except where a month's allocated share lands on a .495 boundary.
THE WHEN IS ALWAYS COMPLETE: ../policyAllocationAppliesInDec is an always-Complete Boolean and the second conjunct is an IsComplete test, so the Switch never collapses to a Placeholder on a return whose allocation intake is half answered.

Fact.Name: This policy's APTC for January, before any Part IV allocation
Fact.Description: This Form 1095-A's own APTC for January, as the Marketplace reported it and as this graph derives it from the annual figure or the monthly entry. It is the figure a policy the filer did NOT share with another taxpayer carries all the way to the return, and the base the Part IV allocation percentage multiplies where the policy IS shared: ../ptcMonthlyAptcPremiumJan is that multiplication, and every reader of this policy's January reads THAT fact, not this one.

PTC repayment limitation, Line 28
A SECOND CASE: PUBLICATION 974'S WORKSHEET X LINE 25 OVERRIDES TABLE 5 FOR THE SIMPLIFIED CALCULATION METHOD POPULATION. The publication says it in one sentence, at its Worksheet X line 25 instruction: "Line 25. Also, enter this amount on line 28 of the Form 8962 you attach to your tax return if you are required to complete that line and you do not complete Worksheet Y. Do not enter an amount from Table 5 in the Form 8962 instructions." (p974 :3246-3250). The reason is that the limitation is a function of household income, and on this return household income was figured with the method's own self-employed health insurance deduction; a Table 5 lookup beside it would apply a cap computed at a different deduction.
WHERE THE CASE SITS. Measured on this tree, the 400-percent-or-more case is the LAST case of this Switch, so a case placed after it would be unreachable for every percent below 400: the under-200, under-300 and under-400 Table 5 cases all match first, and those are exactly the returns the override is for. The case is therefore placed IMMEDIATELY AFTER /taxFamilySizeIsZero and BEFORE the Table 5 bands, and it carries LessThan(/householdIncomeAsPercent, 400) itself so that a return at or above 400 percent still falls through to the shipping $0. Same semantics, reachable placement.
THE CONJUNCTS. IsComplete(/netPtcAmountWhenNegative) is the shipping "required to complete that line" test, copied from every Table 5 case beside it: line 28 is only reached when line 27 shows excess advance payments. form7206:/pub974SimplifiedMethodApplies and form7206:/pub974WorksheetXApplies are the publication's own two conditions - the method must apply, and Worksheet X must actually have been completed (p974 :3200, Worksheet X is filled out "only if APTC was paid to your insurer on your behalf for the months you were self-employed"). "You do not complete Worksheet Y" holds by construction here: Worksheet Y is the alternative for a filer claiming one of the Special Instructions deductions, and every one of those is a member of scheduleSE:/pub974CoordinationResidual, which the method selector requires to be Complete and false.
NO NEW EDGE AND NO CYCLE. This fact already reads /householdIncomeAsPercent in every case below, and form7206:/pub974WorksheetXLine25RepaymentLimitation is measured clean of /potentiallyApplicableTaxPayer, /agi, /householdIncome, /ptcMagi and scheduleSE:/selfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction.
THE PERCENT THIS CASE TESTS IS THE FINAL ONE, not the interim one, and that is deliberate: line 28 is a line of the FILED Form 8962, whose line 5 is the final /householdIncomeAsPercent. Worksheet X lines 18, 21 and 24 select the CAP at the method's own percents; whether line 28 is required at all is a question about the filed return.
TWO THINGS THIS FACT SHOULD RECORD. (1) This case reads form7206:/pub974WorksheetXApplies BARE, which would normally be a Placeholder risk. It is self-protecting here: the only way that fact goes Incomplete is the Worksheet W line 2 chain, and the same chain makes /netPtcAmountWhenNegative Incomplete, so the FIRST conjunct IsComplete(/netPtcAmountWhenNegative) is Complete-false before the bare read is ever evaluated. (That chain is also a member of scheduleSE:/pub974CoordinationResidual, so such a return is refused outright.) (2) The LessThan(..., 400) guard was attacked with twenty-one crafted returns whose final line 5 is 401. In every one it held and this fact came back $0.00 through the shipping 400-percent-or-more case, even where Worksheet X line 25 was carrying 4,200 - which matters, because Worksheet X line 25's own fourth route returns the WHOLE attributable advance payment rather than a cap when its line 24 is 400 or more, and that figure must never reach a line 28 the filer is required to complete. The guard was not PROVED unreachable, only unbroken on everything the review could build.
DO NOT LAND THIS CASE WITHOUT THE SCHEDULE 1 LINE 17 ARM. An override on Form 8962 with no line 17 counterpart on the same return is the unwitnessed posture this wave was twice bitten by; it landed in the same commit as scheduleSE:/selfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction's simplified-method case and the fourth arm of scheduleSE:/knockoutSelfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction narrowing.

Fact.Name: Form 8962 Table 4 question 1: both spouses unmarried on January 1
Fact.Description:
Whether the filer and their spouse were EACH unmarried on the first day of the tax year — Table 4's first eligibility question for the alternative calculation for year of marriage, and the only one of the five that says "you married DURING this year" rather than "you are married now".
WHY IT IS ASKED RATHER THAN DERIVED: filers:/isMarried is year-end status under section 7703(a)(1), and no marriage DATE exists anywhere in dictionary/ty2025. It is a different quantity from hsa's per-month married-status vector, which falls back to the year-end status when unanswered.
SCREEN SPECIFICATION. QUESTION TEXT: "Were you and your spouse each unmarried on January 1, 2025?" HELP TEXT: "Answer yes only if neither of you was married to anyone on the first day of the year. If you married during the year you may be able to elect the alternative calculation for year of marriage, which can reduce the advance premium tax credit you have to pay back" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8962.pdf, page 13). ASKED WHEN: the return is married filing jointly and advance payments of the premium tax credit were made. UNANSWERED POSTURE: read as NO by /ptcBothUnmarriedOnJan1, so the alternative calculation is not offered — the source requires a yes to all five Table 4 questions to elect, and a filer who is not offered the election files the ordinary calculation rather than being refused. VALIDATION: yes or no. WHAT IT FEEDS: /ptcBothUnmarriedOnJan1 and through it /potentiallyEligibleForAltCalcBecauseMarriedThisYear, the Part V election gate.

Fact.Name: Table 4 question 1, complete safe
Fact.Description: /writablePtcBothUnmarriedOnJan1 when it was answered, and NO otherwise. The fallback is what keeps /potentiallyEligibleForAltCalcBecauseMarriedThisYear Complete on every return that has not been asked, and it falls the way the source does: Table 4 requires a yes to elect.

Fact.Name: The month the filer got married
Fact.Description:
The month of the tax year in which the filer and their spouse married. It is the month Publication 974's alternative calculation turns on: the PRE-MARRIAGE MONTHS are the months up to and including it ("Your pre-marriage months include the month you got married"), and the FIRST FULL MONTH OF MARRIAGE is the month after it, which is the month Table 4 question 4 measures enrollment against.
SCREEN SPECIFICATION. QUESTION TEXT: "In which month of 2025 did you get married?" HELP TEXT: "Pick the month your marriage took place. If you married on July 15, your first full month of marriage was August, and January through July are your pre-marriage months" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8962.pdf, page 13; 2025 Publication 974, https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p974.pdf, page 39). ASKED WHEN: /writablePtcBothUnmarriedOnJan1 is yes. UNANSWERED POSTURE: Table 4 question 4 cannot be tested, so /ptcCoverageBeforeFirstFullMonthOfMarriage reads NO and the alternative calculation is not offered; the return files the ordinary calculation rather than being refused. VALIDATION: one of the twelve months of the tax year. WHAT IT FEEDS: /ptcMarriageMonthAsInt, /ptcCoverageBeforeFirstFullMonthOfMarriage, and through them the Part V election gate; Publication 974's Worksheets I through V, when they are built, split every monthly figure at this month.

Fact.Name: The month of marriage as a month number
Fact.Description: /writablePtcMarriageMonth read as 1 through 12, so that the pre-marriage months can be compared against it. INCOMPLETE when the month is unanswered; every reader goes through /ptcCoverageBeforeFirstFullMonthOfMarriage, which is Complete either way.

Fact.Name: Table 4 question 4: someone was enrolled before the first full month of marriage
Fact.Description:
Whether any Form 1095-A policy on this return was active in a PRE-MARRIAGE month — the months up to and including the month of marriage, which are exactly the months before the first full month of marriage. Table 4's example is the definition: married on July 15 means the first full month of marriage is August, so January through July are the months this fact looks at.
TYPE: Boolean, ALWAYS Complete, and the FIRST arm is what makes that true rather than the last one: every other When is an Equal against /ptcMarriageMonthAsInt, and an Equal on an Incomplete operand clears the Switch, so an unguarded body would be Placeholder on exactly the returns that have not answered the month. The first arm answers NO there. NO IS NOT A FREE PASS: an unanswered month means Table 4 question 4 is UNPROVEN, so the election is not OFFERED, and /ptcProvenIneligibleForAltCalc does NOT read this fact for its answered-no proof — a filer who elected and left the month blank stays refused rather than being computed on the method they declined.
WHAT IT APPROXIMATES, stated rather than hidden: Table 4 asks whether anyone in the TAX FAMILY was enrolled in a qualified health plan, and this graph tests whether a Form 1095-A policy was ACTIVE for the month (/hasActive1095APolicyIn...). A policy active in a pre-marriage month with nobody in the tax family on it is not a case this dictionary can currently distinguish, because coverage-family-per-policy identification does not exist here.

Fact.Name: The return is PROVEN not to qualify for the alternative calculation for year of marriage
Fact.Description:
Whether this return can be shown, from ANSWERED facts, to fail Form 8962 Table 4. It is the negative of the eligibility gate and it is deliberately NOT that gate's Not(): an unproven return is not an ineligible one.
WHY THE DISTINCTION IS THE WHOLE POINT. /wantsToUseAltCalculations is a flow knockout that protects a filer who ELECTED an alternative calculation this graph cannot perform. If the knockout keyed on the eligibility gate, an elector who simply has not answered Table 4 yet would fall out of the gate, out of the knockout, and be filed on the ordinary method they declined — a silent substitution of one computation for another. So the knockout keys on this fact instead, and every arm below requires an ANSWERED fact: not filing jointly, not married at year end, advance payments answered NO, no excess advance payment to reduce at all, Table 4 question 1 answered NO, or question 1 answered YES with the month of marriage ANSWERED and no policy active in any pre-marriage month.
TYPE: Boolean, ALWAYS Complete: every arm is either an IsComplete test or a fact that is itself always Complete, so the knockout that reads it can never go Incomplete.

Fact.Name: The five Table 4 eligibility questions this graph can test
Fact.Description:
Whether the return may elect the alternative calculation for year of marriage. It carries four of Table 4's five questions: question 1, both spouses unmarried on January 1 (/ptcBothUnmarriedOnJan1 — the "you married DURING the year" test); question 2, married at year end (filers:/isMarried, which is year-end status under section 7703(a)(1)); question 3, filing jointly; question 4, someone enrolled before the first full month of marriage (/ptcCoverageBeforeFirstFullMonthOfMarriage); and question 5, APTC paid (/hasAdvancedPtc). The IsComplete on /netPtcAmountWhenNegative is Worksheet 3's own precondition — the election only ever matters where there is excess APTC to reduce.
ALL FIVE QUESTIONS ARE LOAD BEARING. Question 1 is the only one that means MARRIED DURING THIS YEAR: filers:/isMarried is year-end status under section 7703(a)(1), so without question 1 this gate would admit every long-married joint filer with advance payments to an election they cannot make.
THIS FACT IS THE OFFER GATE, not the refusal. The application shows the Part V election question when it is true. The refusal /wantsToUseAltCalculations keys on /ptcProvenIneligibleForAltCalc instead, because an elector who has not answered Table 4 yet is UNPROVEN, not ineligible, and must stay refused rather than be filed on the method they declined.
(writable)Whether the TP wants to use the alt calculations for excess APTC

Fact.Name: The filer elected the alternative calculation for year of marriage
Fact.Description:
Whether the filer both MAY elect the alternative calculation for year of marriage and has elected it. It is a flow knockout, and a protective one: Publication 974's Worksheets I through V are not built, so a return that elects cannot be computed here and is refused rather than silently computed on the ordinary method the filer declined.
IT KEYS ON PROOF OF INELIGIBILITY, NOT ON THE ELIGIBILITY GATE, and the difference is the whole safety of the refusal. /potentiallyEligibleForAltCalcBecauseMarriedThisYear is the OFFER gate: it goes false the moment a Table 4 answer is missing. Keying the knockout on it would take an elector who simply has not answered Table 4 yet out of the refusal and file them on the ordinary method they declined. /ptcProvenIneligibleForAltCalc goes true only on an ANSWERED failure, so the refusal holds until the return can be SHOWN not to qualify.
Both operands are always Complete and the read of the writable is IsComplete-guarded, so this fact is always Complete: an Incomplete member of flow.xml's knockout roll-up would turn /flowIsKnockedOut into a Placeholder for the whole return rather than a clean false.
The TP is not have a qualifying plan and is not a non MFJ dependent TP

Fact.Name: Form 8962 Part IV policy amount allocations
Fact.Description: The Form 8962 Part IV allocations of policy amounts, one item per printed allocation row. Part IV prints up to four rows, lines 30 through 33, each carrying columns (a) through (g) for one allocation of one Form 1095-A policy shared with another taxpayer; dictionary/pdf/2025/column-axes.tsv declares the (IRS8962, /form8962PolicyAllocations, rows, 4) axis this collection feeds. The graph has no such collection today. Print only until /needsAllocations stops knocking the return out and becomes the Part IV render gate over this intake.

Fact.Name: Form 8962 Part IV column (g): advance PTC allocation percentage, in thousandths of a percent
Fact.Description:
THE NUMERIC COLUMN (g) INTAKE, declared under the PTC group rulings as the successor to this same path's former shape: a Writable String carrying the raw filer answer ("0.40" for 40%). A String cannot be arithmetic and this graph has no Rational or percentage writable type — the same reason /form1099Rs/*/writableBox9aPercentageThousandths exists — so the percentage the Part IV allocation arithmetic needs has to be DECLARED as an integer rather than typed as the printed decimal.
THE UNIT IS THOUSANDTHS OF A PERCENT, the box 9a/box 8 convention: 40 percent is 40000, 0.5 percent is 500, 100 percent is 100000 and that is the Max. ../advancePtcAllocationPercentageAsRational divides this by 1000 to recover percent units, and ../advancePtcAllocationFraction divides that by 100 to recover the 0-to-1 fraction the credit arithmetic actually multiplies by.
SCREEN SPECIFICATION. QUESTION TEXT: "What percentage of the advance payments of the premium tax credit (APTC) for this policy are you allocating to yourself?" HELP TEXT: "Enter your allocation percentage as a decimal rounded to two places (for example, for 80%, enter 0.80). You and the other taxpayer must allocate the enrollment premiums, the SLCSP premium and the APTC using the SAME percentage; if you do not agree on a percentage, each of you allocates 50% of each amount" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8962.pdf, pages 18, 22). ASKED WHEN: this allocation row's situation requires allocating the APTC for this policy (Allocation Situations 1 through 4 each name which columns apply; the situation selector is upstream of this collection). UNANSWERED POSTURE: left blank on the printed return — "Otherwise, leave column (g) blank" (i8962 line 1479) — this fact stays Incomplete rather than defaulting, and Incompleteness propagates through ../advancePtcAllocationFraction to the printed ../advancePtcAllocationPercentagePrinted cell, which prints blank exactly as the source requires. VALIDATION: an integer from 0 to 100000 inclusive — i8962 itself asks for "a decimal rounded to two places" (i.e. whole-percent-times-1000 granularity, a multiple of 1000 thousandths), and this Int accepts any integer in range, finer than the source ever authorizes; the application's screen should constrain entry to that granularity even though nothing in the fact graph itself rejects a finer answer, because the print fact rounds it away regardless (next sentence). ../advancePtcAllocationPercentagePrinted rounds to two decimal places via AsDecimalString's own HALF_UP convention (confirmed by this stage's own form8962-part4-percentage-half-up-rounding fixture: 32.5% prints "0.33", the exact-half case rounding away from zero), so the printed cell always satisfies the source's two-decimal rule regardless of the intake's extra headroom. WHAT IT FEEDS: ../advancePtcAllocationPercentageAsRational, thence ../advancePtcAllocationFraction, the multiplier /sharedPolicyAllocatedAmounts applies to this policy's APTC, and the printed Form 8962 Part IV column (g).

Fact.Name: Form 8962 Part IV column (g) percentage as a number, in percent units
Fact.Description: ../writableAdvancePtcAllocationPercentageThousandths divided by 1000. 40000 becomes the Rational 40, which is 40 PERCENT and not the fraction two-fifths — ../advancePtcAllocationFraction is the fraction. INCOMPLETE when the intake is unanswered, deliberately: every reader goes through ../advancePtcAllocationFraction or the printed cell, both of which stay Incomplete in that case.

Fact.Name: Form 8962 Part IV column (g) percentage as the fraction the APTC allocation multiplies by
Fact.Description: ../advancePtcAllocationPercentageAsRational over 100. 40 percent becomes the Rational 0.40, the operand /sharedPolicyAllocatedAmounts multiplies this policy's APTC by, and the operand the printed ../advancePtcAllocationPercentagePrinted cell renders at two decimal places. INCOMPLETE when the intake is unanswered, which is the correct blank-cell posture (i8962 line 1479, "Otherwise, leave column (g) blank").

Fact.Name: Form 8962 Part IV column (g): advance PTC allocation percentage, as printed
Fact.Description:
Column (g) of an allocation row AS PRINTED: the advance PTC allocation percentage rendered as a decimal rounded to two places ("for 80%, enter 0.80", i8962 line 1478). DERIVED, not answered directly here — RETIRED as a Writable String under the PTC group rulings, because a String cannot be arithmetic. The filer's answer now lives at the numeric ../writableAdvancePtcAllocationPercentageThousandths, and this fact is AsDecimalString at scale 2 of ../advancePtcAllocationFraction. Resolves Incomplete, and prints blank, exactly when the intake is unanswered — the source's own "leave column (g) blank" case.
RENAMED from ../writableAdvancePtcAllocationPercentage: a "writable"-prefixed name on a Derived fact reds lint_fact_paths.py's U4 rule, and an allowlist row is out of scope here. `dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS8962/en/configuration.yml` cell f2_7 and its three sibling-row cells are updated in the same commit to address this new path. AsDecimalString's own rounding is HALF_UP, confirmed by this stage's own form8962-part4-percentage-half-up-rounding fixture on the SLCSP twin (32.5% prints "0.33", not "0.32" — the exact-half case rounds away from zero, not to even).

Fact.Name: Form 8962 Part IV column (c): allocation start month
Fact.Description: Column (c) of an allocation row, the first month the filer is allocating policy amounts. The instructions print the entry as a two digit month of the tax year, "01" for January, so the box holds a month rather than a full date and is a String on the Form 8962 line 35 column (c) precedent. Print only until /needsAllocations stops knocking the return out and becomes the Part IV render gate over this intake.

Fact.Name: Form 8962 Part IV column (d): allocation stop month
Fact.Description: Column (d) of an allocation row, the last month the filer is allocating policy amounts. The instructions print the entry as a two digit month of the tax year, "06" for June, so the box holds a month rather than a full date and is a String on the Form 8962 line 35 column (d) precedent. It closes the range opened by column (c). Print only until /needsAllocations stops knocking the return out and becomes the Part IV render gate over this intake.

Fact.Name: Form 8962 Part IV column (b): SSN of the other taxpayer
Fact.Description: Column (b) of an allocation row, the SSN of the taxpayer with whom the filer is allocating the policy amounts. The instructions note this SSN may or may not appear on the filer's own Form 1095-A, so it is an intake, not a read of an existing fact. Typed TIN, the graph's type for a taxpayer identifying number. Print only until /needsAllocations stops knocking the return out and becomes the Part IV render gate over this intake.

Fact.Name: Form 8962 Part IV column (a): Marketplace policy number
Fact.Description: Column (a) of an allocation row, the Marketplace assigned policy number of the shared Form 1095-A policy, copied from Form 1095-A line 2. The instructions cap it at fifteen characters: if the policy number is longer, only the last fifteen are entered. A String because the number is an identifier, not a quantity. Print only until /needsAllocations stops knocking the return out and becomes the Part IV render gate over this intake.

THE NUMERIC COLUMN (f) INTAKE, declared under the PTC group rulings as the successor to this same path's former shape: a Writable String carrying the raw filer answer ("0.67" for 67%). THE UNIT IS THOUSANDTHS OF A PERCENT, the box 9a/box 8 convention: 67 percent is 67000, 0.5 percent is 500, 100 percent is 100000 and that is the Max. ../slcspAllocationPercentageAsRational divides this by 1000 to recover percent units, and ../slcspAllocationFraction divides that by 100 to recover the 0-to-1 fraction the credit arithmetic actually multiplies by.
SCREEN SPECIFICATION. QUESTION TEXT: "What percentage of the applicable SLCSP premium for this policy are you allocating to yourself?" HELP TEXT: "Enter your allocation percentage as a decimal rounded to two places (for example, for 67%, enter 0.67). You will enter an allocation percentage here only if you allocated the policy amounts under Allocation Situation 1 or Allocation Situation 4; in every other situation you instead determine the correct applicable SLCSP premium for your own coverage family and enter that amount directly on Form 8962 lines 12 through 23, column (b). You and the other taxpayer must allocate the enrollment premiums, the SLCSP premium and the APTC using the SAME percentage; if you do not agree on a percentage, each of you allocates 50% of each amount" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8962.pdf, pages 18, 22). ASKED WHEN: this allocation row's situation requires allocating the applicable SLCSP premium for this policy. UNANSWERED POSTURE: left blank on the printed return — "leave column (f) blank because you do not allocate the applicable SLCSP premium" (i8962 lines 1464-1465) — this fact stays Incomplete rather than defaulting, and Incompleteness propagates through ../slcspAllocationFraction to the printed ../slcspAllocationPercentagePrinted cell, which prints blank exactly as the source requires. VALIDATION: an integer from 0 to 100000 inclusive — i8962 itself asks for "a decimal rounded to two places" (i.e. whole-percent-times-1000 granularity, a multiple of 1000 thousandths), and this Int accepts any integer in range, finer than the source ever authorizes; the application's screen should constrain entry to that granularity even though nothing in the fact graph itself rejects a finer answer, because the print fact rounds it away regardless (next sentence). ../slcspAllocationPercentagePrinted rounds to two decimal places via AsDecimalString's own HALF_UP convention, confirmed directly here by form8962-part4-percentage-half-up-rounding: 32.5% (thousandths 32500) prints "0.33", not "0.32" — the exact-half case rounds away from zero, not to even — so the printed cell always satisfies the source's two-decimal rule regardless of the intake's extra headroom. WHAT IT FEEDS: ../slcspAllocationPercentageAsRational, thence ../slcspAllocationFraction, the multiplier /sharedPolicyAllocatedAmounts applies to this policy's applicable SLCSP premium, and the printed Form 8962 Part IV column (f).

Fact.Name: Form 8962 Part IV column (f) percentage as a number, in percent units
Fact.Description: ../writableSlcspAllocationPercentageThousandths divided by 1000. 67000 becomes the Rational 67, which is 67 PERCENT and not the fraction — ../slcspAllocationFraction is the fraction. INCOMPLETE when the intake is unanswered, deliberately: every reader goes through ../slcspAllocationFraction or the printed cell, both of which stay Incomplete in that case.

Fact.Name: Form 8962 Part IV column (f) percentage as the fraction the SLCSP allocation multiplies by
Fact.Description: ../slcspAllocationPercentageAsRational over 100. 67 percent becomes the Rational 0.67, the operand /sharedPolicyAllocatedAmounts multiplies this policy's applicable SLCSP premium by, and the operand the printed ../slcspAllocationPercentagePrinted cell renders at two decimal places. INCOMPLETE when the intake is unanswered, which is the correct blank-cell posture (i8962 lines 1464-1465).

Fact.Name: Form 8962 Part IV column (f): applicable SLCSP allocation percentage, as printed
Fact.Description:
Column (f) of an allocation row AS PRINTED: the applicable SLCSP allocation percentage rendered as a decimal rounded to two places ("for 67%, enter 0.67", i8962 line 1456). DERIVED, not answered directly here — RETIRED as a Writable String under the PTC group rulings, because a String cannot be arithmetic. The filer's answer now lives at the numeric ../writableSlcspAllocationPercentageThousandths, and this fact is AsDecimalString at scale 2 of ../slcspAllocationFraction. Resolves Incomplete, and prints blank, exactly when the intake is unanswered — the source's own "leave column (f) blank" case.
RENAMED from ../writableSlcspAllocationPercentage: a "writable"-prefixed name on a Derived fact reds lint_fact_paths.py's U4 rule, and an allowlist row is out of scope here. `dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS8962/en/configuration.yml` cell f2_6 and its three sibling-row cells are updated in the same commit to address this new path. AsDecimalString's own rounding is HALF_UP, confirmed directly here by form8962-part4-percentage-half-up-rounding: 32.5% (thousandths 32500) prints "0.33", not "0.32" — the exact-half case rounds away from zero, not to even.

Fact.Name: The Form 8962 Part IV allocation row that splits this policy
Fact.Description:
The item of /form8962PolicyAllocations that allocates this Form 1095-A's policy amounts between the filer and another taxpayer. FILER SUPPLIED, and it has to be: the printed form joins the two by having the filer copy the policy number from Form 1095-A line 2 into Part IV column (a), and string equality on that number is not a join this engine expresses.
WHY THE LINK POINTS THIS WAY. The consumer is the 1095-A, whose monthly enrollment premium, applicable SLCSP premium and APTC are the three amounts the row's percentages divide, so the element that needs to know names its row. An allocation row cannot be found from the policy it describes without a reverse lookup this engine does not express, exactly as at scheduleE:/rentalProperties/*/linkedSection179AllocationRow.
SCREEN SPECIFICATION. QUESTION TEXT: "Which allocation applies to this health plan?" HELP TEXT: "You entered one allocation row for each policy you shared with another taxpayer. Pick the row whose Marketplace-assigned policy number matches the policy number on this Form 1095-A, line 2" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8962.pdf, page 21). ASKED WHEN: the return has at least one item in /form8962PolicyAllocations and this Form 1095-A is one of the shared policies. UNANSWERED POSTURE: this policy is not allocated at all — every monthly amount passes through whole, which is the correct answer for a policy the filer did not share. VALIDATION: one item of /form8962PolicyAllocations; the application should offer the rows by their column (a) policy numbers. WHAT IT FEEDS: ../policyAllocationRowResolves, the twelve ../policyAllocationAppliesIn... month tests, and through them this policy's twelve monthly enrollment premiums, applicable SLCSP premiums and APTC amounts.

Fact.Name: This policy's allocation start month as a month number
Fact.Description: Form 8962 Part IV column (c) of the allocation row this policy links to, read as a month number: the first month the filer is allocating policy amounts, "01" through "12" on the printed form, 1 through 12 here. The column is a String because the form prints a two digit month, and a String cannot be compared against a month, so this Switch is the one place the two representations meet. INCOMPLETE when the link is unanswered, when the column is unanswered, or when the answer is not one of the twelve two digit months — all three are the same thing to every reader, which is why ../policyAllocationRowResolves takes IsComplete of this fact rather than of the String.

Fact.Name: This policy's allocation stop month as a month number
Fact.Description: Form 8962 Part IV column (d) of the allocation row this policy links to, read as a month number: the last month the filer is allocating policy amounts, "01" through "12" on the printed form, 1 through 12 here. The column is a String because the form prints a two digit month, and a String cannot be compared against a month, so this Switch is the one place the two representations meet. INCOMPLETE when the link is unanswered, when the column is unanswered, or when the answer is not one of the twelve two digit months — all three are the same thing to every reader, which is why ../policyAllocationRowResolves takes IsComplete of this fact rather than of the String.

Fact.Name: This policy's Part IV allocation link reaches a usable month range
Fact.Description:
Whether ../linkedPolicyAllocationRow reaches a row this graph can actually apply: the link is answered AND both of its month columns read as months. All three terms are needed. An unanswered CollectionItem dereferences to nothing, and a row that exists with a blank or unreadable column (c) or (d) would otherwise hand the policy an allocation over an undefined range.
TYPE: Boolean, ALWAYS Complete, and that is load bearing rather than tidy. This fact is read in Switch When clauses by the twelve ../policyAllocationAppliesIn... tests and by /anyPolicyAllocationResolves, and an Incomplete in a When clears the Switch's completeness flag, which would turn every monthly premium Placeholder on every return that answers a Form 1095-A. All three terms are IsComplete tests, so none of them can be Incomplete. The same argument is written out at scheduleE:/rentalProperties/*/section179AllocationRowResolves, which this fact copies.
WHAT IT DOES NOT TEST: the three allocation percentages. A blank column is a legitimate answer the source states — column (f) is entered only under Allocation Situations 1 and 4, and column (g) only where the situation allocates APTC — so each percentage is tested for completeness at the amount that multiplies it, and a blank column leaves that one amount whole.

Fact.Name: This policy's Part IV allocation covers January
Fact.Description:
Whether the allocation row linked to this Form 1095-A applies to January: the link resolves AND column (c) is January or earlier AND column (d) is January or later. The allocation runs only over the months columns (c) and (d) name, not the whole year, so a policy shared from January through July is split for seven months and whole for the other five.
TYPE: Boolean, ALWAYS Complete. It is read in a Switch When by this policy's January enrollment premium, applicable SLCSP premium and APTC, so an Incomplete here would turn all three Placeholder. The first arm answers false whenever ../policyAllocationRowResolves is false, and inside the second arm both month numbers are Complete by that fact's own construction.

Fact.Name: The Part IV row linked to this policy carries at least one allocation percentage
Fact.Description:
Whether the allocation row this Form 1095-A links to has answered any of its three percentage columns. ANY of the three, not all three, and that is what the source says rather than a weakening of it: a column is entered only where the allocation situation allocates that amount — column (f) only under Allocation Situations 1 and 4, column (g) only where the situation allocates the APTC, and Allocation Situation 2 enters column (g) alone and leaves (e) and (f) blank. So a row with one answered column is a complete allocation, and a row with none is not an allocation at all.
TYPE: Boolean, ALWAYS Complete — three IsComplete tests under an Any, read in Switch When clauses and in Filter predicates.

Fact.Name: This policy's Part IV allocation row names a month range that contains no month
Fact.Description:
The link resolves to a row whose column (c) is LATER than its column (d) — an allocation that applies to no month of the year. It is a contradictory intake, not an absent one, and the difference decides where it is counted: /allocationIntakeIsComplete counts it into the ZERO bucket beside ../policyAllocationPercentagesMissing, so /needsAllocations keeps refusing the return. Reading it through ../policyAllocationRowResolves instead would make the row say "this policy is not allocated" and pass the whole policy amount through — the silent 100 percent allocation this module refuses to make, on a return that has told the graph the policy is shared and is printing a filled Part IV row beside it.
WHY start > stop IS EXACTLY "no month": both endpoints are months 1 through 12 by construction (../policyAllocationStartMonthAsInt and ../policyAllocationStopMonthAsInt are Incomplete for anything else, and then the row does not resolve at all), so if start is not after stop the month equal to start is inside the range.
TYPE: Boolean, ALWAYS Complete — ../policyAllocationRowResolves is, and inside its true arm both month numbers are Complete by that fact's own construction.

Fact.Name: This policy carries a Part IV allocation this graph can apply
Fact.Description:
The link resolves to a row that carries at least one allocation percentage AND whose month range contains at least one month. It is the per-policy half of the test that decides whether the return's Part IV intake is finished; /allocationIntakeIsComplete counts it.
TYPE: Boolean, ALWAYS Complete — all three conjuncts are.

Fact.Name: This policy names a Part IV allocation row that allocates nothing
Fact.Description:
The link resolves to a row with a readable month range and that row's three percentage columns are ALL unanswered. It is the half-answered intake the knockout must keep refusing: reading it as "no allocation" would hand the filer the whole policy amount, which is a silent 100 percent allocation of a policy they have told this graph they share.
TYPE: Boolean, ALWAYS Complete.

Fact.Name: This return has Part IV allocation rows that no Form 1095-A uses
Fact.Description:
Whether /form8962PolicyAllocations holds more rows than there are Forms 1095-A naming one. Two intakes land here and both are contradictory rather than absent: a row the filer entered and never attached to a policy (it prints in Part IV and touches no amount), and a SECOND row for a policy that already names one (a Form 1095-A carries one ../linkedPolicyAllocationRow, so the extra row is silently unused, which is i8962's "more than one allocation for a single policy" case). Both count into /allocationIntakeIsComplete's refusal, so /needsAllocations keeps the return rather than filing a Part IV whose printed rows and computed amounts disagree.
TYPE: Boolean, ALWAYS Complete, and the first arm is why. CollectionSize over the raw /form8962PolicyAllocations does NOT resolve on a return with no allocation collection at all — the same trap /ptcCanReportAnnualTotals documents for /1095As — so the raw count is read only inside the arm where at least one row resolves, which cannot happen unless the collection exists.

Fact.Name: Form 8962 line 9: allocating policy amounts, or electing the year-of-marriage calculation
Fact.Description:
Form 8962 line 9 as printed: "Are you allocating policy amounts with another taxpayer or do you want to use the alternative calculation for year of marriage?" It is Yes when this return actually allocates — at least one Form 1095-A names an allocation row this graph can apply — or when the year-of-marriage election is in play.
WHY IT READS WHAT PART IV SHOWS RATHER THAN THE TRIGGER QUESTIONS. /isAdditionalPersonPartofDifferentTaxFamily and /isEnrolledWithOtherFamily are the filer's answers to the CONDITIONS line 9's instruction states (i8962 lines 750 to 772); /anyPolicyAllocationResolves is whether Part IV is filled in. A printed line 9 must agree with the Part IV rows printed under it and with the allocated amounts printed on lines 12 through 23, so this fact reads the latter. THE CONTRADICTION CASE IS NAMED, NOT REFUSED: a return that answered both trigger questions NO and then linked an allocation row prints line 9 Yes over a Part IV the filer's own answers say is unnecessary. Nothing in this dictionary reconciles the two, because the triggers are return-level and name no policy; the return is not refused for it, since every printed figure is internally consistent.
The second leg cannot fire on a filed return today and is declared anyway, because it is half of what the printed line asks: /wantsToUseAltCalculations is a flow knockout, so a return electing the alternative calculation does not reach print at all. When Publication 974's Worksheets I through V are built and that refusal retires, this line already says the right thing.
TYPE: Boolean, ALWAYS Complete — both operands are.

Fact.Name: Form 8962 line 9: the No box — not allocating policy amounts and not electing the year-of-marriage calculation
Fact.Description: The negation of /form8962Line9AllocatingPolicyAmountsOrUsingAltCalc, declared as its own fact because the printed line 9 is a Yes/No checkbox pair and the PDF register binds one fact per box (dictionary/pdf/2025/IRS8962/en/configuration.yml, c1_4[1]; the scheduleC line G pair /writableMateriallyParticipated and /didNotMateriallyParticipated is the precedent). Nothing else reads it. TYPE: Boolean, ALWAYS Complete — its operand is. Exported like its Yes-box twin: the register is its only consumer, and lint_wiring reads a print binding as no consumer.

Fact.Name: This return's Form 8962 Part IV intake is finished
Fact.Description:
Whether a return that needs Part IV has actually supplied it: at least one Form 1095-A names an allocation row this graph can apply; no Form 1095-A names a row that allocates nothing, either because none of its three percentage columns is answered or because its month range is empty (column (c) later than column (d)); and no allocation row is left over with no Form 1095-A using it. It is the narrowing term on both allocation knockouts — /needsAllocations and /dependentTpRequiresAllocations each keep refusing exactly the returns where this is false, which is the data-completeness residue rather than the whole allocation population.
WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT TEST, because this graph cannot, in two parts. (1) The ALLOCATION SITUATION. i8962's Table 3 sorts a return into one of four situations, and which columns must be answered follows from that — Situation 2 answers column (g) alone, Situations 1 and 4 answer column (f), Situation 3 does not allocate the APTC. No fact in this dictionary asks which situation applies, so a row answering one column is accepted as complete and the "all three amounts using the same percentage" rule of Situation 1 is not enforced.
(2) WHICH POLICIES ARE SHARED. The three triggers that say an allocation is needed (/isAdditionalPersonPartofDifferentTaxFamily, /isEnrolledWithOtherFamily, and the dependent-taxpayer legs) are RETURN LEVEL: none of them names a Form 1095-A. So on a return with two policies, one linked to a usable allocation row and one not, this fact is true and the unlinked policy keeps its whole amount — which is right if that policy was never shared and wrong if it was. The "never a silent 100 percent" guarantee this fact makes is therefore per-POLICY-that-names-a-row and per-return-with-no-row, not per-shared-policy, and closing the gap needs a per-1095-A "shared with another taxpayer" answer (or the allocation-row collection made the single source of truth for which policies are shared). Both gaps are named here rather than papered over with a guess.
TYPE: Boolean, ALWAYS Complete: both counts are taken over Filters, which yield 0 and stay Complete on a return with no Form 1095-A at all.

Fact.Name: At least one Form 1095-A on this return is allocated in Part IV
Fact.Description:
Whether any Form 1095-A links to a Part IV allocation row this graph can apply. It is the Form 8962 line 10 test the instructions state directly: "If you complete Part IV, check “No” on line 10", so a return that allocates cannot report annual totals on line 11 and must complete the monthly lines 12 through 23. /ptcCanReportAnnualTotals takes Not of this fact as a conjunct.
TYPE: Boolean, ALWAYS Complete, because the count is taken over a Filter rather than over the raw collection: a Filter over an absent /1095As yields 0 and stays Complete, where a CollectionSize over the bare collection would go Incomplete on every return with no Marketplace policy. The same argument is written out on /ptcCanReportAnnualTotals itself.

Fact.Name: Form 8962 line 35a alternative family size
Fact.Description: Alternative family size the primary filer enters on Form 8962 line 35 column (a) when electing the alternative calculation for year of marriage. It is the pre marriage family size, which differs from /taxFamilySize because the spouse and the spouse's dependents are left out for the pre marriage months. Print only until the Part V election gate exists.

Fact.Name: Form 8962 line 36a alternative family size for the spouse
Fact.Description: Alternative family size the spouse enters on Form 8962 line 36 column (a) when the couple elects the alternative calculation for year of marriage. Line 36 is the spouse's own row, a separate scalar entry from the primary filer's line 35, not another item of a collection. Print only until the Part V election gate exists.

Fact.Name: Form 8962 line 35b alternative monthly contribution amount
Fact.Description: Alternative monthly contribution amount the primary filer enters on Form 8962 line 35 column (b) under the alternative calculation for year of marriage. It replaces the line 8b monthly contribution amount for the pre marriage months, so it is not /ptcMontlyContributionAmount. Print only until the monthly contribution facts consume it.

Fact.Name: Form 8962 line 36b alternative monthly contribution amount for the spouse
Fact.Description: Alternative monthly contribution amount the spouse enters on Form 8962 line 36 column (b) under the alternative calculation for year of marriage. It replaces the line 8b monthly contribution amount for the spouse's pre marriage months. Print only until the monthly contribution facts consume it.

The printed box holds a month of the tax year, not a full date, and it delimits which coverage months use the line 35 alternative entries. Print only until the Part V election gate exists.

Fact.Name: Form 8962 line 36c alternative start month for the spouse

Line 36 is the spouse's own row, a separate scalar entry from the primary filer's line 35, not another item of a collection. The printed box holds a month of the tax year, not a full date, so it is a String on the line 35 column (c) precedent, and it delimits which coverage months use the line 36 alternative entries. Print only until the Part V election gate exists.

Fact.Name: Form 8962 line 35d alternative stop month
Fact.Description: Last month of the alternative calculation period the primary filer enters on Form 8962 line 35 column (d). The printed box holds a month of the tax year, not a full date, and it closes the range opened by line 35 column (c). Print only until the Part V election gate exists.

Fact.Name: Form 8962 line 36d alternative stop month for the spouse
Fact.Description: Last month of the alternative calculation period the spouse enters on Form 8962 line 36 column (d). Line 36 is the spouse's own row, a separate scalar entry from the primary filer's line 35, not another item of a collection. The printed box holds a month of the tax year, not a full date, so it is a String on the line 35 column (d) precedent, and it closes the range opened by line 36 column (c). Print only until the Part V election gate exists.

Fact.Name: Form 8962 line 2b dependents modified AGI
Fact.Description:
Form 8962 line 2b: the COMBINED modified AGI of the filer's dependents who are required to file their own income tax return, transcribed by the filer from Worksheet 1-2. It is the second addend of household income under IRC 36B(d)(2)(A), and /householdIncome reads it through the complete-safe wrapper /ptcDependentsModifiedAgiOrZero.
ONE ATTESTED TOTAL, NOT A PER-DEPENDENT SUM, and that is a deliberate boundary rather than a shortcut: this dictionary collects a dependent's relationship, age and residency on familyAndHousehold, and no income of theirs at all — no AGI, no tax-exempt interest, no nontaxable social security, and no filing-threshold determination. Worksheet 1-2 is a worksheet the filer runs against returns this graph never sees, so the figure enters as the filer's own total. A per-dependent shape on the familyAndHousehold dependent collection is a successor unit, not this fact.
SCREEN SPECIFICATION. QUESTION TEXT: "What is the combined modified adjusted gross income of your dependents who have to file their own tax return?" HELP TEXT: "Add up the modified AGI of every dependent you are claiming who is required to file an income tax return because their income meets the filing threshold. Use Worksheet 1-2 in the Form 8962 instructions to work out each dependent's modified AGI — it is their AGI plus any excluded foreign earned income, tax-exempt interest, and the untaxed part of their social security benefits. TWO THINGS TO LEAVE OUT: a dependent who is filing ONLY to claim a refund of tax withheld or estimated tax is not counted at all ("Do not include the modified AGI of dependents who are filing a tax return only to claim a refund of tax withheld or estimated tax", https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8962.pdf, page 8); and if you are filing Form 8814 for a child and its line 4 is more than $1,350, Worksheet 1-2 line 1 takes specific amounts from Form 8814 instead of that child's own return — the tax-exempt interest from line 1b, the lesser of line 4 or line 5, and any nontaxable social security the child received" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8962.pdf, page 8). ASKED WHEN: the filer has a PTC-qualifying plan, claims at least one dependent, and has answered /writableDependentsRequiredToFile yes. UNANSWERED POSTURE: the return is REFUSED rather than defaulted — /dependentsRequiredToFile keeps knocking out exactly the return that says a dependent must file and does not give the figure, because /ptcDependentsModifiedAgiOrZero would otherwise read it as $0 and understate household income, which overstates the credit. A filer who answers /writableDependentsRequiredToFile no is never asked and the $0 is correct for them. VALIDATION: a whole dollar amount, zero or more. WHAT IT FEEDS: /ptcDependentsModifiedAgiOrZero, /householdIncome (Form 8962 line 3, "Add lines 2a and 2b"), and through it the applicable figure, the contribution amount and the whole premium tax credit.

Fact.Name: Interim household income is below 100 percent of the poverty line with no advance payments
Fact.Description:
The INCOME half of the Publication 974 stop: whether the household income Step 1 of the simplified calculation method figures (form7206:/pub974Step1HouseholdIncome) is below 100 percent of the federal poverty line for the tax family, on a return with no advance payments of the premium tax credit.
WHY IT IS A STOP AND NOT A SELECTOR. A taxpayer below 100 percent of the poverty line is not an applicable taxpayer under IRC 36B(c)(1)(A), so no credit is allowed, and Publication 974's own answer for a filer who cannot take the credit is an ORDINARY Form 7206 rather than the method ("Cannot take the PTC. If you are not eligible to take the PTC, stop here. Do not use this method." p974 :3521-3526), which this dictionary reaches through form7206:/pub974FallbackApplies. But this test is a function of household income, which is a function of the self-employed health insurance deduction the method computes, so it cannot gate the method that produces it. It is therefore read ONLY by scheduleSE:/pub974CannotTakePtcStop, which is read only by scheduleSE:/knockoutSelfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction. No Worksheet W, Worksheet X, Step or interim fact and no selector may read it, and none does.
WHY THE NO-ADVANCE-PAYMENTS CONJUNCT. IRC 36B(c)(1)(B) and the Form 8962 instructions treat a taxpayer whose household income falls below 100 percent of the poverty line as an applicable taxpayer anyway when advance payments were made for the enrollment, so the below-100-percent case is only a stop when no advance payment was made. /hasAdvancedPtc is read as "known and false OR not known": an unanswered advance-payment question leaves the return in the refusal rather than out of it, which is the conservative direction for a knockout operand.
THE TAX-FAMILY-SIZE-ZERO CASE. /federalPovertyLevelThreshold is $0 when the tax family is empty, and every income is at or above $0, so without the first case a childless non-filer shape would read as "not below 100 percent" for an accidental reason rather than a considered one. The first case answers false explicitly and says why here.
UNBUILT NEIGHBOUR, NAMED. The other two members of the stop live in scheduleSE:/pub974CannotTakePtcStop: /qualifiedForPtc false on the finished return and /wantsToUseAltCalculations. This fact is the only one of the three that needed a new computation.

Fact.Name: Interim Form 8962 line 5: Step 1 household income as a percent of the poverty line
Fact.Description:
Form 8962 line 5 on the INTERIM Form 8962 of Publication 974's Simplified Calculation Method: Step 1 household income expressed as a percentage of the federal poverty line for the tax family, rounded down to a whole percent. The twin of ptc:/householdIncomeAsPercent, which is untouched and remains the figure the FILED Form 8962 prints on line 5.
THE INTERIM PASS, in one paragraph. Publication 974's Simplified Calculation Method figures the deduction in three steps: Step 1 figures household income using Worksheet X line 31 (or Worksheet W line 17) as the self-employed health insurance deduction, Step 2 runs a Form 8962 "only through line 24" on THAT household income and does NOT attach it to the return, and Step 3 turns that line 24 into Schedule 1 line 17. This fact is one line of Step 2's INTERIM Form 8962. It is a twin of the shipping fact of the same quantity, re-parameterised on form7206:/pub974Step1HouseholdIncome instead of on ptc:/householdIncome, and NOTHING IT COMPUTES IS EVER PRINTED: the Form 8962 the return files is the shipping chain, computed on the final household income. p974 :3518-3519 says the Step 2 Form 8962 is not attached to the return.
WHY A TWIN RATHER THAN A READ. Every input of this fact is measured free of ptc:/potentiallyApplicableTaxPayer, /agi, /householdIncome, /ptcMagi and scheduleSE:/selfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction. That is the whole reason the twin exists: the shipping quantity is a function of the deduction the method is computing, so reading it would close the cycle the Simplified Calculation Method is prescribed to avoid.
THE 401 SHORTCUT IS KEPT, DELIBERATELY. The shipping fact answers a flat 401 whenever household income exceeds four times the poverty line instead of computing the ratio, and this twin does the same. THE REASON IS NOT that 401 is the right number here; it is that a twin must be the SAME FUNCTION as the fact it twins evaluated at a different household income, or no later author can reason about one from the other. NOTHING IS LOST BY KEEPING IT: the only consumer of this fact is /pub974InterimApplicableFigure, whose top band is FLAT at 0.085 for every value at or above 400 (IRC 36B(b)(3)(A)(iii)'s table, "400.0 percent and higher" 8.5 to 8.5), so 401 and the true ratio select the same applicable figure and produce the same interim credit to the cent. AND NOTHING IS MISREPORTED BY KEEPING IT: line 5 of the Form 8962 the filer signs is the shipping /householdIncomeAsPercent, which this fact does not touch, and the Step 2 Form 8962 this fact belongs to is never attached (p974 :3518-3519). Dropping the shortcut would have changed no figure and would have made two facts that differ in exactly one operand differ in two.
THE TAX-FAMILY-SIZE-ZERO CASE is kept for the same reason and does the same work as on the shipping fact: /federalPovertyLevelThreshold is $0 on an empty tax family, and a division by zero is neither a computation nor a refusal.
COMPLETE-SAFETY. Every case is a comparison of Complete operands or a True default, so this fact is Complete on every return. It is read only by the applicable-figure twin, which is read only through facts the method selector gates.

Fact.Name: Interim Form 8962: the applicable figure at Step 1 household income
Fact.Description:
The applicable figure (Form 8962 instructions Table 2) for the INTERIM Form 8962 of Publication 974's Simplified Calculation Method. The twin of ptc:/applicableFigure, and a PURE RE-PARAMETERISATION of it: the body below is the shipping body with every read of /householdIncomeAsPercent replaced by /pub974InterimHouseholdIncomeAsPercent and nothing else changed, five bands and the odd/even parity sub-switch included. It was produced mechanically from the shipping body rather than retyped, so the two cannot drift in band boundaries or in the interpolation constants.
THE INTERIM PASS, in one paragraph. Publication 974's Simplified Calculation Method figures the deduction in three steps: Step 1 figures household income using Worksheet X line 31 (or Worksheet W line 17) as the self-employed health insurance deduction, Step 2 runs a Form 8962 "only through line 24" on THAT household income and does NOT attach it to the return, and Step 3 turns that line 24 into Schedule 1 line 17. WHY A TWIN RATHER THAN A READ. Every input of this fact is measured free of ptc:/potentiallyApplicableTaxPayer, /agi, /householdIncome, /ptcMagi and scheduleSE:/selfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction. That is the whole reason the twin exists: the shipping quantity is a function of the deduction the method is computing, so reading it would close the cycle the Simplified Calculation Method is prescribed to avoid.
WHY THE PARITY SUB-SWITCH IS COPIED RATHER THAN SIMPLIFIED. In the 300-to-399 band the shipping fact adds 0.00005 when the interpolation step lands on an odd tenth, which is how the printed Table 2 rounds. It is a rounding convention of the table, not of the household income, so it applies identically to an interim percent; and re-deriving it here would be a second spelling of the same quantity, which the records refuse.
COMPLETE-SAFETY. The Switch is exhaustive over the Int this fact reads (at most 150, at most 300, at most 399, at least 400), and that Int is Complete on every return, so this fact is too.

Fact.Name: Interim Form 8962 line 11d: annual maximum premium assistance
Fact.Description:
Form 8962 line 11d on the INTERIM Form 8962: annual maximum premium assistance, the annual benchmark premium less the interim annual contribution amount, floored at $0. The twin of ptc:/annualMaxPremiumAssitance (the shipping path carries a typo; the twin does not reproduce it).
THE ONE CASE THE TWIN DOES NOT COPY, and why. The shipping fact opens with All(IsComplete(/potentiallyApplicableTaxPayer), Not(/potentiallyApplicableTaxPayer)) answering $0, landed by stage 0b under operator ruling (b''). This twin OMITS it, for a reason that has to be stated because omitting an applicability test looks like a defect. (a) It could not be copied: /potentiallyApplicableTaxPayer is a function of household income and so of the very deduction this method is computing, and every measurement in this unit is that no interim fact may read it. (b) It is not needed: the interim pass is read only through form7206:/pub974SimplifiedMethodApplies, which already requires ptc:/maybeEligibleForPtc, Not(/notPtcApplicableTaxPayerSoFar) and Not(/filerNotQualifiedForPtcBecauseOfStatusAndResidenceInfo) - the three NON-income applicability tests - and the remaining, income-based half of applicability is refused by scheduleSE:/pub974CannotTakePtcStop through the knockout, which is the only place it can live without a cycle. (c) Nothing this fact computes is printed: the FILED Form 8962 line 11d is still the shipping fact, with its PAT case intact.

Fact.Name: Interim Form 8962 Part II column (d) for January: maximum premium assistance
Fact.Description:
Form 8962 Part II column (d) for January on the INTERIM Form 8962: the benchmark premium for the month less the interim monthly contribution amount, floored at $0. The twin of ptc:/monthlyPtcMaxPremiumAssitanceForJan (the shipping path carries a typo; the twin does not reproduce it).
THE INTERIM PASS, in one paragraph. Publication 974's Simplified Calculation Method figures the deduction in three steps: Step 1 figures household income using Worksheet X line 31 (or Worksheet W line 17) as the self-employed health insurance deduction, Step 2 runs a Form 8962 "only through line 24" on THAT household income and does NOT attach it to the return, and Step 3 turns that line 24 into Schedule 1 line 17. THE ROUTE GATE, and why it is not the shipping one. The shipping monthly facts gate on All(/needsToFileForm8962Monthly, /hasActive1095APolicyInJan). /needsToFileForm8962Monthly is All(/mayNeedToFileForm8962, Not(/ptcCanReportAnnualTotals)) and its first conjunct REACHES /potentiallyApplicableTaxPayer and through it /agi, so the interim twin cannot read it. The twin gates on All(/hasPtcQualifyingPlan, Not(/ptcCanReportAnnualTotals), /hasActive1095APolicyInJan) instead: all three are measured clean, /ptcCanReportAnnualTotals is the annual/monthly route switch itself, and /hasPtcQualifyingPlan replaces the applicability half of /mayNeedToFileForm8962 so that a return with no Form 1095-A leaves this fact Incomplete exactly as the shipping fact does rather than minting a Complete $0.
WHY THE BENCHMARK IS SUMMED INLINE. ptc:/monthlyPtcSlcspPremiumForJan is the shipping fact for this column (b) figure, and it is measured DIRTY for the same reason: it is gated on /needsToFileForm8962Monthly. Its body is Round(CollectionSum(/1095As/*/ptcMonthlySlcspPremiumJan)), which is what appears inline here; the item-level path is measured clean. That is the idiom plan v2 section C.2 prescribes for the interim pass, and it mints no second fact for a quantity the shipping dictionary already names.
THE PAT CASE IS OMITTED for the reason set out in full on /pub974InterimAnnualMaxPremiumAssistance: it cannot be read without a cycle, the method selector already carries the three non-income applicability tests, and the income half is the knockout's through scheduleSE:/pub974CannotTakePtcStop.
COMPLETE-SAFETY. No default: Incomplete on the annual route and on a return with no policy active in January, which is what the shipping fact does.
