THE ROUTE GATE, and why it is not the shipping one. The shipping monthly facts gate on All(/needsToFileForm8962Monthly, /hasActive1095APolicyInJan). /needsToFileForm8962Monthly is All(/mayNeedToFileForm8962, Not(/ptcCanReportAnnualTotals)) and its first conjunct REACHES /potentiallyApplicableTaxPayer and through it /agi, so the interim twin cannot read it. The twin gates on All(/hasPtcQualifyingPlan, Not(/ptcCanReportAnnualTotals), /hasActive1095APolicyInJan) instead: all three are measured clean, /ptcCanReportAnnualTotals is the annual/monthly route switch itself, and /hasPtcQualifyingPlan replaces the applicability half of /mayNeedToFileForm8962 so that a return with no Form 1095-A leaves this fact Incomplete exactly as the shipping fact does rather than minting a Complete $0. The disallowed-coverage-month conjunct is the shipping fact's own third conjunct, Not(/anyPolicyDisallowsCoverageMonthInJan), copied unchanged and measured clean: a month whose enrollment premium went unpaid by the due date is not a coverage month (IRC 36B(c)(2)(A)(ii)) and earns no credit.
WHY THE ENROLLMENT PREMIUM IS SUMMED INLINE. ptc:/monthlyPtcPremiumForJan carries this column (a) figure and is DIRTY through /needsToFileForm8962Monthly; its body is Round(CollectionSum(/1095As/*/ptcMonthlyPremiumJan)), which appears inline here, over an item-level path measured clean.
COMPLETE-SAFETY. No default: Incomplete on the annual route, on a return with no policy active in January, and on a month the return disallows, which is what the shipping fact does. The Step 3 consumers read it through an IsComplete Switch that reads an Incomplete month as $0.

Fact.Description:
Form 8962 Part II column (e) for February on the INTERIM Form 8962: the lesser of the month's enrollment premiums and the interim maximum premium assistance for the month. The twin of ptc:/monthlyPtcAllowedForFeb.
THE INTERIM PASS, in one paragraph. Publication 974's Simplified Calculation Method figures the deduction in three steps: Step 1 figures household income using Worksheet X line 31 (or Worksheet W line 17) as the self-employed health insurance deduction, Step 2 runs a Form 8962 "only through line 24" on THAT household income and does NOT attach it to the return, and Step 3 turns that line 24 into Schedule 1 line 17. This fact is one line of Step 2's INTERIM Form 8962. It is a twin of the shipping fact of the same quantity, re-parameterised on form7206:/pub974Step1HouseholdIncome instead of on ptc:/householdIncome, and NOTHING IT COMPUTES IS EVER PRINTED: the Form 8962 the return files is the shipping chain, computed on the final household income. p974 :3518-3519 says the Step 2 Form 8962 is not attached to the return.

WHY THE ENROLLMENT PREMIUM IS SUMMED INLINE. ptc:/monthlyPtcPremiumForOct carries this column (a) figure and is DIRTY through /needsToFileForm8962Monthly; its body is Round(CollectionSum(/1095As/*/ptcMonthlyPremiumOct)), which appears inline here, over an item-level path measured clean.
COMPLETE-SAFETY. No default: Incomplete on the annual route, on a return with no policy active in October, and on a month the return disallows, which is what the shipping fact does. The Step 3 consumers read it through an IsComplete Switch that reads an Incomplete month as $0.

Fact.Name: Interim Form 8962 Part II column (e) for November: premium tax credit allowed
Fact.Description:
Form 8962 Part II column (e) for November on the INTERIM Form 8962: the lesser of the month's enrollment premiums and the interim maximum premium assistance for the month. The twin of ptc:/monthlyPtcAllowedForNov.
THE INTERIM PASS, in one paragraph. Publication 974's Simplified Calculation Method figures the deduction in three steps: Step 1 figures household income using Worksheet X line 31 (or Worksheet W line 17) as the self-employed health insurance deduction, Step 2 runs a Form 8962 "only through line 24" on THAT household income and does NOT attach it to the return, and Step 3 turns that line 24 into Schedule 1 line 17. This fact is one line of Step 2's INTERIM Form 8962. It is a twin of the shipping fact of the same quantity, re-parameterised on form7206:/pub974Step1HouseholdIncome instead of on ptc:/householdIncome, and NOTHING IT COMPUTES IS EVER PRINTED: the Form 8962 the return files is the shipping chain, computed on the final household income. p974 :3518-3519 says the Step 2 Form 8962 is not attached to the return.
WHY A TWIN RATHER THAN A READ. Every input of this fact is measured free of ptc:/potentiallyApplicableTaxPayer, /agi, /householdIncome, /ptcMagi and scheduleSE:/selfEmployedHealthInsuranceDeduction. That is the whole reason the twin exists: the shipping quantity is a function of the deduction the method is computing, so reading it would close the cycle the Simplified Calculation Method is prescribed to avoid.

COMPLETE-SAFETY. No default: Incomplete on the annual route, on a return with no policy active in November, and on a month the return disallows, which is what the shipping fact does. The Step 3 consumers read it through an IsComplete Switch that reads an Incomplete month as $0.

Fact.Name: Interim Form 8962 line 24: total premium tax credit (Step 2)
Fact.Description:
Form 8962 LINE 24 on the INTERIM Form 8962: the total premium tax credit the Simplified Calculation Method's Step 2 figures. The twin of ptc:/totalPtcAmountAllowed, and the fact Step 3 line 2 reads ("Enter the total PTC (Form 8962, line 24) you figured in Step 2, earlier", p974 :3489-3490).

The monthly arm's gate is All(/hasPtcQualifyingPlan, Not(/ptcCanReportAnnualTotals)) where the shipping fact uses /needsToFileForm8962Monthly, for the reason set out on the monthly facts: the applicability half of /needsToFileForm8962Monthly reaches /potentiallyApplicableTaxPayer and cannot be read here. The qualifying-plan conjunct is what keeps a return with no Form 1095-A Incomplete instead of minting a Complete $0 sum of twelve absent months.
COMPLETE-SAFETY. Each monthly addend is wrapped in the shipping IsComplete Switch, so a month with no coverage contributes $0 rather than poisoning the Add; the outer Switch has no default, so a return that carries no qualified health plan leaves this fact Incomplete.

Fact.Name: Interim Form 8962: the twelve column (e) amounts are the same for each month
Fact.Description:
Whether the twelve column (e) amounts on the INTERIM Form 8962 are the same for every month. This is one half of the test in the Caution under line 1 of Publication 974's Step 3 Worksheet: "If the amounts on lines 12 through 23, column (e), of your Step 2 Form 8962 are not the same for each month and you had specified premiums for less than 12 months, skip lines 2 through 5 below and enter on line 6 the total of those column (e) amounts for the months you paid specified premiums." (p974 :3481-3488). The other half is the specified-month count, which form7206:/pub974SpecifiedMonthCount already carries; the two are joined in form7206:/pub974Step3Line6PtcAllocableToSpecifiedPremiums.
WHY THE ANNUAL ROUTE IS TRUE. On the annual route the Step 2 Form 8962 reports line 11 and leaves lines 12 to 23 blank, so there are no per-month column (e) amounts to be unequal and the Caution cannot fire. Answering TRUE is the reading that sends such a return down lines 2 to 5, which is the route the publication's own worked example takes.
HOW AN ABSENT MONTH IS READ, and it is a decision rather than a mechanism. A month with no coverage leaves the interim column (e) fact Incomplete; each comparison below reads that as $0. So a policy that runs for part of the year is NOT uniform, and a return with fewer than twelve specified months therefore takes the Caution route and sums the actual column (e) amounts for its specified months rather than prorating an annual total. That is the conservative reading and it is the one the Caution exists to force: proration by month count is only right when every month carries the same credit.
COMPLETE-SAFETY. Every operand is wrapped so that Incomplete reads as $0 and the Switch has a True default, so this fact is Complete on every return, including one with no Form 1095-A (where the annual-totals test is false, every month is $0, and the answer is TRUE vacuously - harmless, because the consumer is gated on the method selector).

Fact.Name: Employer-sponsored coverage periods by person
Fact.Description: One row per tax-family member and period with the same employer-plan terms. MonthSets preserve the person/month grain required by IRC 36B(c)(2)(C).

Fact.Description: Name or unique household label for the individual. FILER SUPPLIED.

Fact.Description: Months this row's terms were available to the individual. FILER SUPPLIED MonthSet.

Fact.Name: Months the person was enrolled in employer coverage
Fact.Description: Months the individual was actually covered, the clause-(iii) arm that disqualifies the month without applying affordability or minimum-value tests. FILER SUPPLIED MonthSet.

Fact.Name: Lowest-cost self-only required monthly contribution
Fact.Description: The employee's monthly contribution for the lowest-cost self-only plan available for this period, before the health-flex reduction. FILER SUPPLIED Dollar with cents.

Fact.Name: Monthly health-flex contribution reducing required contribution
Fact.Description: The monthly employer flex contribution that Publication 974 directs the filer to subtract from the required contribution. Optional; unanswered contributes zero.

Fact.Name: Required monthly contribution after health-flex reduction
Fact.Description: Lowest-cost self-only required contribution less an answered health-flex contribution, floored at zero. Dollar arithmetic preserves cents.

Fact.Name: Employer plan provides minimum value
Fact.Description: Whether the plan pays at least 60 percent of allowed costs and provides substantial inpatient and physician coverage, as stated by the employer's SBC or Form 1095-C indicator.

Fact.Name: Marketplace determined the employer offer unaffordable at enrollment
Fact.Description: The at-enrollment safe-harbor determination. FILER SUPPLIED Boolean; unanswered must not be treated as either affordable or unaffordable by the future monthly calculation.

Fact.Description: The single month to which this row's three Dollar amounts apply.

Fact.Description: The portion IRC 36B(e)(1)(A) removes from column (a). FILER SUPPLIED.

Fact.Name: Form 1095-A VOID box
Fact.Description: The VOID checkbox at the top of the form (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1095a.pdf, page 2). Checked means an earlier Form 1095-A for the policy in Part I was sent in error and neither form's information is used to figure the premium tax credit on Form 8962 (Instructions for Recipient, same file lines 141-146, LEFT column). A checked box blocks the return until the VOID form and the earlier form for that policy are deleted (/1095As/*/voidBoxChecked, /tpNeedsToDelete1095A), so a voided document never reaches the Form 8962 sums. Unanswered it reads as not checked. WHAT IT FEEDS: /1095As/*/voidBoxChecked; also stored for the state returns that reconcile a state marketplace subsidy or read the recipient's coverage, and bound in the Form 1095-A register.

Fact.Name: Form 1095-A CORRECTED box
Fact.Description: The CORRECTED checkbox at the top of the form (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1095a.pdf, page 2). Checked means this form replaces an earlier one for the same policy and only this form's information is used (Instructions for Recipient, same file lines 147-151, LEFT column). Unanswered it is complete-safe: nothing in this module reads it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal; stored for the state returns that reconcile a state marketplace subsidy or read the recipient's coverage, and bound in the Form 1095-A register.

Fact.Name: Form 1095-A Part II covered individuals
Fact.Description: Form 1095-A Part II, Covered Individuals (lines 16-20), as a collection nested under one received Form 1095-A (one policy): one item is one covered individual, in the order the form lists them. The register prints item i on printed row i (dictionary/pdf/2025/column-axes.tsv), and a covered individual past the fifth prints on a continuation statement (dictionary/pdf/2025/continuations.tsv). SCREEN: add one entry for each person listed in Part II of this Form 1095-A, top to bottom, and transcribe columns A through E as printed (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1095a.pdf, page 2). When the Marketplace sends an additional Form 1095-A that only continues Part II for a policy with more than five covered individuals (same file lines 129-130, RIGHT column), add those people here as further entries of the same policy; the continuation is not a second policy. ASKED WHEN: the filer enters a Form 1095-A. VALIDATION: any number of entries. UNANSWERED: complete-safe; an unanswered list has not been transcribed and is not an assertion that the form lists nobody. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal; Form 8962 reads the Part III amounts, not Part II, and no Form 1040 line reads it. Exported for the state returns that reconcile a state marketplace subsidy; no module under dictionary/states/ reads it at this revision. Bound in the Form 1095-A register.

Fact.Name: Form 1095-C documents

Fact.Name: Form 1095-C document owner
Fact.Description: The primary or secondary filer to whom this Form 1095-C is addressed as employee. An unanswered owner is Incomplete; no primary-filer default is assumed. This link supplies ownership for the two attribution facts, not another copy of the printed identifying number.

Fact.Name: Form 1095-C belongs to primary filer
Fact.Description: Whether this Form 1095-C belongs to the primary filer. The owner link and the corresponding filer must both be complete before they are compared. An unanswered owner or an absent primary filer produces false. No federal tax computation reads this attribution; it is exported for document ownership.

Fact.Name: Form 1095-C belongs to secondary filer
Fact.Description: Whether this Form 1095-C belongs to the secondary filer. The owner link and the corresponding filer must both be complete before they are compared. An unanswered owner or an absent secondary filer produces false. No federal tax computation reads this attribution; it is exported for document ownership.

Fact.Name: Form 1095-C box 2 employee's social security number
Fact.Description: Form 1095-C Part I box 2, "Social security number (SSN)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1095c.pdf, page 1), DERIVED from this item's own employee (../filer): the primary filer's TIN on the primary filer's form, the secondary filer's TIN on the spouse's form, never the return's primary filer by default. /form1095Cs carries a filer link, so INPUT-FORMS section (c)'s identity rule makes the ADDRESSEE'S number a derivation, not a writable; every covered individual's TIN in Part III column (b) stays a writable, because a covered individual is not on this return by construction. The employer may print only the last four digits on the employee copy; this fact is the full number the return already holds. Nothing to ask: the employee screen (../filer) decides it. Unanswered ../filer leaves it Incomplete, which is complete-safe: nothing reads it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal. Exported for state systems and bound in the Form 1095-C register.

Fact.Name: Form 1095-B documents
Fact.Description: Source documents received on Form 1095-B, one item per received document. The collection records the printed document without computing or changing federal tax. Its items are available for state returns and document transcription.

Fact.Name: Form 1095-B document owner
Fact.Description: The primary or secondary filer to whom this Form 1095-B is addressed as responsible individual. An unanswered owner is Incomplete; no primary-filer default is assumed. This link supplies ownership for the two attribution facts, not another copy of the printed identifying number.

Fact.Name: Form 1095-B belongs to primary filer
Fact.Description: Whether this Form 1095-B belongs to the primary filer. The owner link and the corresponding filer must both be complete before they are compared. An unanswered owner or an absent primary filer produces false. No federal tax computation reads this attribution; it is exported for document ownership.

Fact.Name: Form 1095-B belongs to secondary filer
Fact.Description: Whether this Form 1095-B belongs to the secondary filer. The owner link and the corresponding filer must both be complete before they are compared. Fact.Name: Form 1095-B box 2 responsible individual's SSN or other TIN
Fact.Description: Form 1095-B Part I box 2, "Social security number (SSN) or other TIN" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1095b.pdf, page 1), and the same cell reprinted in the page-3 continuation header (same file line 118), DERIVED from this item's own responsible individual (../filer): the primary filer's TIN on the primary filer's form, the secondary filer's TIN on the spouse's form, never the return's primary filer by default. /form1095Bs carries a filer link, so INPUT-FORMS section (c)'s identity rule makes the ADDRESSEE'S number a derivation, not a writable; every covered individual's TIN in Part IV column (b) stays a writable. The issuer may print only the last four digits on the recipient copy; this fact is the full number the return already holds. Nothing to ask: the responsible-individual screen (../filer) decides it. Unanswered ../filer leaves it Incomplete, which is complete-safe: nothing reads it. WHAT IT FEEDS: nothing federal. Exported for state systems and bound in the Form 1095-B register.
